summary: Dutasteride is an oral dual 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor used for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men with an enlarged prostate, reducing prostate volume, improving symptoms and lowering the risk of acute urinary retention and BPH-related surgery. It lowers serum PSA by about 50%, so a new PSA baseline should be established and any confirmed rise evaluated. It is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can harm a male fetus; pregnant women must not handle leaking capsules, and patients must not donate blood until 6 months after the last dose.
indications: Treatment of symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men with an enlarged prostate
Not approved for the prevention of prostate cancer

moa: Dutasteride inhibits the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the androgen primarily responsible for development and enlargement of the prostate. It is a competitive, specific inhibitor of both the type 1 and type 2 isoforms of 5-alpha-reductase, forming a stable, slowly dissociating enzyme complex. It does not bind the human androgen receptor.

absolute: Pregnancy / use in females who are pregnant (may cause harm to a male fetus)
Clinically significant hypersensitivity (e.g. serious skin reactions, angioedema, urticaria, pruritus, respiratory symptoms) to dutasteride or other 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors or any component
relative: Concurrent potent chronic CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, ketoconazole) - use caution
Obstructive uropathy or other urological conditions causing similar symptoms (evaluate before starting)
monitor: Other urological causes of symptoms before initiating

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Dutasteride is a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor that prevents conversion of testosterone to DHT, a hormone necessary for normal development of male genitalia, and can cause abnormalities of the external genitalia in a male fetus. In animal studies dutasteride inhibited normal development of male external genitalia at doses below the maximum recommended human dose. Pregnant women or women who may become pregnant should not handle the capsules because dutasteride is absorbed through the skin.
lact: Dutasteride is not indicated for use in females; there are no data on its presence in human milk.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment.
hepatic: Dutasteride is extensively metabolized by CYP3A4/CYP3A5; its use has not been studied in hepatic impairment. Because exposure may be increased, use with caution in patients with hepatic disease.

major: Potent chronic CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, ketoconazole) - may raise dutasteride exposure; use caution
moderate: Other CYP3A4 inhibitors - potential for increased dutasteride exposure
interactions.food: Food does not affect dutasteride pharmacokinetics; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported with alcohol

missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the usual time; do not take two capsules at once.
overdose: In volunteer trials single doses up to 40 mg (80 times the therapeutic dose) for 7 days and 5 mg daily for 6 months were given without significant safety concerns. There is no specific antidote; give symptomatic and supportive treatment, taking the long half-life of dutasteride into account.
